title: How he came to play the Embers, following Louis Metcalf and Jonah Jones
summary: He played the Embers in the 1960s, following Metcalf and Jonah Jones, in and out with a changing group.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Herman, in the -- back around the 1950's sometime you started playing at the Embers, didn't you?
Fifties? No, it wasn't that far back. No.
How did you first happen to be at the Embers? Because that was, as I recall, a place that mostly featured trumpeters, so you were a natural to go there.
Yes. Yes. Louie Metcalf was one of the first guys I knew to have gone there, and stayed there for a while, in and out. He and Jonah Jones.

And Jonah was the man quite a while and later on, let's see, I'm trying to think now, who mentioned my name, or how I got in there. But I was lucky enough to follow them in there several times. I was in and out of the Embers quite often, I guess like some of the rest of the guys, and we had a lot of fun, and they seemed to enjoy me there, very much.
Did you have a regular group? The same group every time you went in? Or did it change?
No, it changed. If I was lucky enough
to grab the same guys, I did, which is very seldom happens, because you don't know just when the date's going to come up, and whether you'll be here, or there, or with someone else.
